text:
[LCDB.3.2.1.1] **Suppression level.** The
  cooldown gate operates at the **RHS level**, not the
  LHS activation level. The rule continues to activate
  on every matching LHS (Rete propagation, refraction,
  binding capture, all unchanged); the dispatcher's
  `ds-rate-allow` builtin wraps the whole RHS as
  `(if (ds-rate-allow "<rule>" <activation-key>) then
  <body>)`. A within-cooldown activation has its RHS
  short-circuited but still consumes the activation
  budget — refraction tracks it as fired for the
  purposes of LCRS / LCDB.5 interactions. This matters
  for two observable behaviours: (a) `cooldown` does
  not skip pattern-side side effects (capture-let
  evaluation, slot reads) inside the LHS — the LHS
  always runs; (b) the activation key is computed
  every time the LHS matches, not lazily inside the
  gate.

idris.name: lcrs_6_2_1__no_site_run_if
idris.note: With no site, the RHS under a verdict is Rete/NetworkTimed.idr's, over every verdict.

idris.name: lcrs_6_2_1__rhs_gated_called
idris.note: The RHS with calls gated by the rule's cooldown: Rete/NetworkTimed.idr's gate, then the RHS with calls under its verdict.

idris.name: lcrs_6_2_1__run_if_called
idris.note: The RHS with calls under the rule's verdict: admitted, the actions and the sites run from position 0; refused, nothing runs and no call is issued.

idris.name: lcdb_3_2_1_1__allowed_is_the_firing
idris.note: AN ADMITTED FIRING IS THE FIRING: when the gate's verdict on the fired match's key at the clock is `true`, the firing's net is `iret_11_4__fire_ttl_net`'s -- the activation marked, the actions run -- and the trackers gain `(rule, key) -> clock` in front. Over every program, state, selection and table.

idris.name: lcdb_3_2_1_1__rhs_gated
idris.note: `(if (ds-rate-allow "<rule>" <activation-key>) then <body>)`: the gate over the fired match's key at the net's clock, then the body, or nothing. (a) and (b) are not observable in a pure model: the LHS has no side effects and the key, a function of the match, has no computation time -- the model computes it at the gate, which the clause forbids only as an observable.

idris.name: lcdb_3_2_1_1__rhs_once
idris.note: THE RHS GATES ONCE: the trackers after it are the trackers before, or those with the rule's key stamped at the clock in front.

idris.name: lcdb_3_2_1_1__run_if
idris.note: The RHS under a verdict: admitted, the actions run on the marked net; refused, the marked net stands and no action runs -- the RHS short-circuited, the activation marked all the same.

idris.name: lcdb_3_2_1_1__run_if_trackers
idris.note: The trackers after the RHS under a verdict are the verdict's.

idris.name: lcdb_3_2_1_1__suppressed_leaves_memory
idris.note: Marking an activation leaves working memory: the refused firing's net holds the facts it held. A transcription of `idat_6_2_2__mark_net`.

idris.name: lcdb_3_2_1_1__suppressed_runs_no_action
idris.note: A REFUSED FIRING RUNS NO ACTION: when the verdict is `false`, the firing's net is the net with that activation marked fired and nothing else -- working memory, the dependency rows, the deadlines and the clock as they were -- and the trackers are the ones before. Over every program, state, selection and table.

idris.name: lcdb_3_2_1__fire_gated
idris.note: The rule activates on every matching LHS and refraction marks it fired whether or not the gate admits the RHS: the selection and the marking are the plain firing's, and the gate decides the body alone.

idris.name: rdsc_4a_8_2_3__suppressed_is_still_the_firing
idris.note: 'Refraction tracks it as fired': after a within-cooldown activation's firing the activation carries `fired`, and the selection does not take it again.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_4__allowed_is_the_stamped_firing
idris.note: An admitted gate: the actions run after the mark, the admission recorded, on the stamped engine.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_4__fire_timed
idris.note: The rule activates on every matching LHS the sample admits and refraction marks it fired whether or not the gate admits the RHS.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_4__rhs_gated
idris.note: `(if (ds-rate-allow "<rule>" <activation-key>) then <body>)` over the stamped RHS. (a) and (b) are not observable in a pure model, as Rete/NetworkCooldown.idr's `lcdb_3_2_1_1__rhs_gated` says.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_4__run_if
idris.note: The RHS under the gate's verdict at the RHS level: refused, the RHS is short-circuited and the activation, marked before, stays marked.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_4__run_if_drops
idris.note: The RHS-level verdict is the one Rete/NetworkCooldown.idr applies.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_4__suppressed_runs_no_action
idris.note: 'A within-cooldown activation has its RHS short-circuited': no action runs, the activation is marked, nothing else moves.
